extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors of Wolters Kluwer / Lippincott journals
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level ethical policies and practical requirements for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and managing scholarly journal manuscripts for Wolters Kluwer / Lippincott journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: WKH commitments to publishing ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: WKH is committed to fostering editorial independence, supporting editors to set policies and run journals ethically and transparently, and maintaining an accurate and transparent academic record, including publishing corrections and retractions when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the publisher's overarching expectations and institutional responsibilities toward editorial independence, transparent policies, and correction of the record; underpins all subsequent policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide guidelines to authors for manuscript preparation and submission; establish a system for effective and rapid peer review; make editorial decisions with reasonable speed and communicate them clearly; establish policies for handling academic misconduct or systemic error requiring correction; communicate all editorial policies and standards clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must operationalize and communicate policies, run timely and effective peer review, and have processes to investigate and act on misconduct or errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the confidentiality of the review process; provide unbiased feedback in a timely manner addressing appropriate aspects of the work; alert the editor to any potential personal financial conflict of interest and decline to review when such a conflict exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should preserve confidentiality, avoid conflicts of interest, be timely, and focus reviews on appropriate scientific and ethical aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure submitted work is original and not previously published or submitted elsewhere; cite sources clearly and obtain permissions; confirm the work does not infringe rights (privacy, IP); report conflicts of interest accurately; communicate material errors to the editor immediately; represent authorship accurately and ensure all credited authors participated and consented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must guarantee originality, proper attribution and permissions, transparent conflict disclosures, timely correction of errors, and accurate authorship attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (ICMJE)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered an author, individuals must meet all four ICMJE criteria: (1) substantial contributions to conception or design, or acquisition/analysis/interpretation of data; (2) drafted the work or revised it critically for important intellectual content; (3) provided final approval of the version to be published; (4) agreed to be accountable for all aspects of the work, ensuring integrity and resolution of questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone meeting all four criteria should be named as an author; those who do not meet all criteria may be acknowledged with permission. Some journals may have additional authorship requirements—check journal-specific policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI — authorship and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: AI authoring tools do not meet ICMJE authorship standards. Authors who use AI tools in writing, producing images/graphics, or in data collection/analysis must transparently disclose in Methods (or similar) how and which tool was used. Authors remain fully responsible and liable for all content, including AI-produced parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must state the tool and how it was used. Authors must not list AI as an author. Authors must not upload accepted or published manuscripts (or parts) into generative AI tools where copyright/licensing might be violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI — editorial and reviewer use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted manuscripts are confidential; editors, editorial staff, and reviewers must not upload submitted manuscripts or parts into generative AI tools, nor upload reviews/decision letters into AI tools, because of confidentiality, proprietary rights, and potential data privacy concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/reviewers must not rely solely on AI to evaluate or make editorial decisions. AI-powered automation may be used for processing speed or validation provided final decisions are made by humans. Evaluations of misconduct should not rely solely on AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealing an editorial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may appeal editorial decisions if they can demonstrate the peer review process was flawed (e.g., reviewer bias) or that substantive factual errors were made by reviewers or editors. Appeals of rejections must be made by email within 30 days of receipt; a decision on appeal will be made quickly and may involve further peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal processes may vary by journal; decisions on appeal are final. Authors should consult the journal's Instructions for Authors for specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints about peer-review and publication process
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints about how a paper was processed should be raised first with the Editor or Editorial Office; if unresolved, the matter can be referred to the Publisher at Wolters Kluwer Health, and if still unsatisfied, to COPE (if the journal is a member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal websites often list Publisher contacts in 'About the Journal' or 'Journal Info'. Other complaints follow research misconduct processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling allegations of research misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: When serious concerns arise about conduct, validity, or reporting, the journal will follow COPE guidance. Editors will contact authors for response; if unsatisfactory, the authors' institution will be contacted to conduct further investigation. Appropriate actions will follow investigation conclusions; expressions of concern may be issued when public health/clinical practice could be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use COPE flowcharts and retraction guidelines for detailed steps. Inconclusive evidence or ongoing investigations may warrant an expression of concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation manipulation is including references solely to increase citations to the referenced article, where references do not contribute to scholarly content and serve self-promotion or personal gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals (especially those indexed in Web of Science) should review citation data periodically to identify manipulation (e.g., excessive self-citation or unrelated citations). Journals should set self-citation thresholds, provide education on best practice, and establish procedures to respond to misconduct; see COPE for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest — author disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission, all authors must identify potential conflicts in the electronic Copyright Transfer Agreement and within the article. On the title page authors must identify all sources of financial support, list all sponsor names and explain any sponsor role in study design, data collection/analysis, writing, or submission decisions, and disclose any financial involvement that could be a potential conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should err on the side of full disclosure and provide as much information as possible; criteria are based on ICMJE recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest — editor/board recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and Editorial Board members will recuse themselves from oversight, peer review, and decisions on papers where they are an author. A guest editor without conflicts will oversee peer review and editorial decisions for such papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recusal prevents conflicts from influencing editorial decisions; journals must have procedures to appoint alternate editors for conflicted submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Data submission requirements vary by article type; manuscripts reporting clinical trials must contain a data sharing statement per ICMJE. Upon request, authors must provide data supporting their paper for editorial review and retain data and records for several years after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to consult the journal's Instructions for Authors for specific data sharing policies and retention periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical oversight for human and animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts describing experimental studies on humans or animals must supply a statement that the study was approved by an institutional review or ethics committee, and for human studies that subjects gave informed consent. Such approval should be described in the Methods (or similar) section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Declaration of Helsinki and local/institutional requirements; include ethics committee name, approval number/ID where applicable, and statement on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property, permissions, and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manuscript should contain only the authors' original work; all authors must certify the manuscript is a unique submission not under consideration elsewhere and not previously published in part or full (short abstracts at meetings are usually acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must secure written release prior to submission for any copyrighted excerpts, figures, tables, or audio/video files and obtain written releases from patients for names/likenesses; provide copies on request and be responsible for permission fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism definition and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is using others' published or unpublished ideas or words (or other IP) without attribution or permission and presenting them as new and original; intent and effect to mislead the reader as to contributions constitutes plagiarism. This applies to abstracts, grant applications, IRB applications, unpublished or published manuscripts in any format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism is scientific misconduct and will be addressed per COPE standards. If detected before publication, editorial offices will take action following COPE guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication discussion mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication discussion is facilitated via letters to the editor, commentaries, or other article types determined by the journal. Editors may consider proposals for such contributions prior to formal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For guidance on post-publication discussion procedures, consult COPE and the specific journal's instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections, expressions of concern, and retractions — definitions and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Erratum: correct a small but important mistake or omission that does not alter a paper's conclusion. Expression of concern: raise awareness of potential unreliability of an article, sometimes precursor to retraction, used when investigation is ongoing or evidence inconclusive. Retractions: used per COPE to alert readers to redundant publication, plagiarism, peer review manipulation, unauthorized reuse of material/data, copyright infringement, data fabrication, unethical research, or failure to disclose a major competing interest that would have unduly influenced the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals will follow COPE guidelines and the journal's own research misconduct policy when issuing corrections or retractions; consult the journal's policy for specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name change policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals and books will consider name change requests for reasons including gender identity, marriage, divorce, and religious conversion. The publisher will work with the author or product editor to establish identity and consider how much to share the request with other authors and readers. Mechanism for correcting names and discrepancies in authorship lists remains available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests may be handled to protect the requester's safety and privacy. The publisher will also update records held by third parties (indexing agencies, legal deposits) where feasible. Authors are recommended to register with ORCID to link publication records irrespective of name changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising policies for print and web publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Lippincott may reject, refuse, omit, postpone, cancel, or require changes to any advertisement or advertisement order at any time, whether or not accepted; customers are responsible to ensure ads are correct, accurate, and not misleading. Lippincott accepts no responsibility for ad errors, including those caused by changes requested by the customer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher may impose additional conditions and notify the customer. This policy covers publication dates and positioning and provides publisher broad rights to modify or refuse advertisements.
